title: Development and validation of a protocol to determine product perception in relation to the moment of the day
author: Visalli, Plano, et al.

steps.title: Recruit eligible student participants
steps.instruction: Recruit approximately 50 undergraduate students (first‑to‑third year) from the Food Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Agronomic Engineering, and Industrial Engineering programs at the Faculty of Engineering and Agricultural Sciences, Pontificia Universidad Católica Argentina, using the university's online platforms, faculty social media channels, and physical notices on campus bulletin boards; exclude anyone with a diagnosed sleep disorder (treated or untreated) or with an aversion or medical restriction to caramel, lemon, anise, or honey‑mint candies. Enroll a total of 52 participants.

substeps.instruction: Post recruitment announcements on online platforms and social media.
Place physical notices in hallways, libraries, and cafeterias.
Screen volunteers for eligibility criteria and exclusions.
Obtain a final sample of 52 students.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: Before any testing, have each participant read and sign the ethics‑committee‑approved informed consent form.

steps.title: Determine PROP bitterness sensitivity
steps.instruction: In the sensory laboratory (Laboratorio de Análisis Sensorial, PUCA), test each participant’s bitterness sensitivity using PROP solutions at three concentrations: 0.032 mM (1.36 mg/L), 0.32 mM (13.6 mg/L), and 3.2 mM (136 mg/L), following the adaptation of Tepper et al.; conduct the test in individual sensory booths that meet standard sensory evaluation guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the three PROP solutions at the specified concentrations.
Present each solution to the participant in a randomized order.
Record the participant’s detection response for each concentration.

steps.title: Assemble candy kits
steps.instruction: Provide each participant with four labeled plastic bags, each containing four commercially available hard candies in their original packaging: Lemon‑Sour (Arcor, Argentina – sourness), Honey‑Mint (Arcor, Argentina – freshness), Caramel (Arcor, Argentina – sweetness), and Anise (Mondelez, Argentina – bitterness).

steps.title: Define evaluation schedule
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to complete 16 sensory evaluations over four consecutive days, performing one evaluation in each of the following daily time slots: Morning 8:00–10:00 am, Midday 12:00–2:00 pm, Afternoon 4:00–6:00 pm, Evening 8:00–10:00 pm; each day they consume one candy of each type, with the order of presentation arranged by a Latin square design and randomized across participants to balance order effects.

substeps.instruction: Generate a Latin square for the four candy types.
Randomize the Latin square assignment for each participant.

steps.title: Report pre‑evaluation states
steps.instruction: Before each candy rating, have participants rate their current hunger (1 = Satiated/Full to 5 = Hungry), thirst (1 = Not thirsty at all to 5 = Very thirsty), tiredness (1 = Not tired/Active/Alert to 5 = Very tired/Want to sleep), and willingness to perform the task (1 = Not willing at all, 3 = Indifferent, 5 = Very willing) using 5‑point scales.

steps.title: Complete daily sleep journal
steps.instruction: For each of the four study days, participants record in a sleep journal the time they went to sleep the previous night, the time they woke up that day, and whether they took a nap the day before (if yes, indicate its duration).

steps.title: Perform sensory rating
steps.instruction: Using the TimeSens software accessed through a unique, non‑transferable link protected by an individualized code and password, participants rate the intensity of sweetness, sourness, bitterness, freshness, and total flavor for the candy on a 5‑point Rate‑All‑That‑Apply (RATA) scale (0 = not applicable, 1 = applies slightly, …, 5 = applies strongly).

steps.title: Send reminder messages
steps.instruction: Pre‑program WhatsApp messages to remind participants to evaluate the scheduled candy within the designated time window; if a participant misses a window, instruct them to wait until the same window on the following day before resuming the assessment.

substeps.instruction: Create reminder text (e.g., “Do not forget to evaluate the candy scheduled for this moment of the day. Here is your personal link.”).
Schedule messages to be sent shortly before each time slot.

steps.title: Conclude study and compensate
steps.instruction: After a participant has completed all 16 evaluations, provide them with a small gift as a token of appreciation for their participation.
